court: In the High Court of Madras
respondents: District Collector Dharmapuri District and Others
case_number: WP No. 19673 of 2026 and WMP No. 20971 of 2026
advocates: For Petitioner(s) : Mr. A.G. Vedavikas, for Ms. V. Srimathi
For Respondent(s) : Mr. P. Balathandayutham, (for R 1 to R 4)
judgment_text:
Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, praying for issuance of writ of certiorari, to call for the records in Na.Ka. 422/2026/E1 dated 7-5-2026 on the file of the 2nd respondent and quash the same as arbitrary, unjust, whimsical and untenable.

The Order of the Court was delivered by

L. Victoria Gowri, J.:— Seeking to challenge the impugned memo dated 7-5-2026 Na.Ka. 422/2026/E1 passed by the second respondent, this Writ Petition is filed.

2. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that earlier the writ petition in W.P. No. 6678 of 2026 was filed before this Court. By order dated 19-2-2026, this Court after dispensing with notice to the petitioner and other private respondents, had disposed of the said writ petition, directing the respondents therein to conduct survey and demarcate the boundaries of the subject property which was sought for surveying by the petitioner therein after receiving objection, if any, and after considering the same. Pursuant to the said order, the impugned memo has been issued by the second respondent. Challenging the same, the present writ petition has been filed.

3. Though this Court in the aforesaid order had directed the second respondent to receive objections, if any and consider the same, it is also directed to conduct the survey and demarcate the boundaries of the property sought for by the fifth respondent herein. However, the property which is sought for survey by the fifth respondent is the absolute property belonging to the petitioner and the fifth respondent being one of the family members of the petitioner's father's vendor, is raising serious challenge with regard to the title of the property after thirty-five years. A civil suit in O.S. No. 442 of 2024 on the file of the sub-court, Dharmapuri, is also pending with respect to the same property. Suppressing all these facts, an order has been obtained by the fifth respondent behind the back of the petitioner. The petitioner's only anticipation is that without considering the petitioner's objection, the second respondent would proceed to conduct survey.

4. Mr P. Balathandayutham, learned Special Government Pleader, appearing for the respondents 1 to 4 submitted that the impugned memo has been passed only pursuant to the order of this Court passed in W.P. No. 6678 of 2026, wherein, this Court had directed the second respondent/Tahsildar to issue notice to the rival parties and thereafter, to give an opportunity of hearing and receive objections, if any, from rival parties, before survey. The first limb of the said order is complied by issuing this memo and there is no illegality in the same.

5. Heard either sides and carefully perused the materials available on record.

6. As rightly pointed out by the learned Special Government Pleader, it is seen that the impugned memo has been issued pursuant to the order passed by this Court in W.P. No. 6678 of 2026. However, the only anticipation of the learned counsel for the petitioner is that despite the objection from the petitioner, still the second respondent may proceed to survey. In this regard, this Court is inclined to clarify that in respect of the subject property a civil suit in O.S. No. 422/2024 is pending between the petitioner herein and the fifth respondent and other parties. Pending the same, the fifth respondent had filed the Writ Petition in W.P. No. 6678/2026 under the guise of conducting survey of the disputed property. Such an exercise is impermissible.

7. It is made clear that the petitioner may appear before the second respondent with all necessary documents along with the information about the pendency of the civil suit in O.S. No. 442 of 2024 on the file of the sub-court, Dharmapuri and on receiving the same, the second respondent is directed to dispose of the 5th respondent's application for survey by recording the pending of the civil suit and the conduct of survey could be subject to the outcome of the said civil suit. The survey as required by the 5th respondent is directed to be kept in abeyance, pending civil suit mentioned supra.

8. It is also brought to the notice of this Court that the second respondent has required the petitioner to appear with the original documents to substantiate his title over the subject suit property. Since already the original documents are before the trial court, the possibility of producing the same would not arise, and he is directed to produce photo copies of relevant documents.

9. With the above observations and directions, this Writ Petition stands disposed of. No costs. Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petition is also closed.
